The age: The age runs from {rules.start} to the armistice of {rules.end.season|season} {rules.end.year}.
The year runs {rules.seasons|list}, and every nation decides once a season.
The {events.greatWar.name} breaks out in the {events.greatWar.schedule.season|season} of {events.greatWar.schedule.from}.

In {rules.start} every province starts at {rules.setup.unrest} unrest, and every nation with {rules.setup.gold.0} to {rules.setup.gold.1} gold and an army between {rules.setup.army.0|pct} and {rules.setup.army.1|pct} of its listed size.
Heirs: Each heir card offers {rules.heirs|word} heirs, and the player may deal again {rules.rerolls|word} times a game.

Every heir is a rarity and a trait. A {rarities.0.name} or {rarities.1.name} ruler has a bonus and a malus; from {rarities.2.name} on he also brings a one-time bonus at his coronation. The rarer he is, the bigger the bonus and the smaller the malus.
More rerolls will be for sale at ${rules.price.reroll} each; they are not for sale yet.
Reigns: A reign lasts {rules.reign.years.0} to {rules.reign.years.1} years if nothing ends it sooner.
Each year a ruler has a {rules.reign.murder|pct} chance of being assassinated.
A ruler beaten in a war he started, or one that cost him land, abdicates {rules.reign.abdicate|pct} of the time.

Besides a {rulers.flirt.label}, whose reign always ends in one, {rules.reign.crisis|pct} of successions end in civil war, which adds {rules.reign.crisisUnrest} unrest everywhere and lasts {rules.reign.crisisYears.0} to {rules.reign.crisisYears.1} years; meanwhile the army fights at {rules.reign.crisisArmy|frac} strength.
In a nation whose unrest is above {rules.reign.coupUnrest}, the army stages a coup in {rules.reign.coup|pct} of seasons and crowns a ruler of its own choosing: no heir card.
A ruler plans at least {rules.horizon.min} years ahead, and up to {rules.horizon.span} more the more patient he is.
Assassins are conspirators until {rules.reign.anarchists}, and anarchists from then on.
Armies: Every soldier is a worker lost: the work done in fields and factories falls with the size of the army, as if {rules.workers}k men per million people would empty them, but it never falls below {rules.workersMin|pct}.
An army that wins a battle with more than {rules.breakthrough|times} the strength of the other side breaks through and advances twice.
Building: A factory takes {rules.build.factory|word} seasons to build, a fortress {rules.build.fort|word} and {rules.price.fort} gold.
Reforms cost {rules.reform.cost} gold and take away {rules.reform.calm} unrest; they can be passed again after {rules.reform.wait|years}.
Unrest and war: A province with unrest of {rules.unrest.restless} or more is restless; at {rules.unrest.uprising} or more it can rise.

Each season a province's unrest moves {rules.unrest.pull|pct} of the way toward what its conditions call for: {rules.unrest.target.base} in calm times; {rules.unrest.target.foreign} more under a ruler of another people, plus {rules.unrest.target.nationalism} times the strength of nationalism, which is {rules.unrest.nationalism.start} in {rules.start} and grows by one every {rules.unrest.nationalism.years} years; {rules.unrest.target.crisis} more during a civil war, {rules.unrest.target.war} at war and {rules.unrest.target.occupied} while occupied; up to {rules.unrest.target.unsettled} more while it is not yet integrated; and from {rules.unrest.workers.from}, {rules.unrest.workers.perFactory} for every factory (at most {rules.unrest.workers.max}), reaching its full weight over {rules.unrest.workers.years} years.
Weighing a war, a ruler counts {rules.settle|pct} of the time a conquest takes to become integrated.
New nations: A nation born in an uprising starts with {rules.newNation.gold} gold and an army of {rules.newNation.armyPerMillion}k men per million people. It leans to war and plans ahead as its own entry says.

Its relations with the nation it broke from start at {rules.newNation.hostility}, but the two keep the peace for {rules.newNation.truce|span}. A great power on bad terms with the old ruler may guarantee its independence for {rules.newNation.guarantee|span}.

When an uprising wins in a province next to a living nation of its own people, the province joins that nation. Otherwise the province's own fallen nation comes back if it was of the same people, or else the people rises as its nation that was not on the map in {rules.start}, or else as its only nation. A people with several nations and none of them new, like the {peoples.german.name} people, finds no allies.
Alliances: An ally comes to a nation's defence {rules.allies.defend|pct} of the time, and always if it guaranteed that nation's independence. It joins an attack {rules.allies.attack|pct} of the time, and only if the two are on good terms.
A nation has at most {rules.allies.max|word} allies. An alliance between nations on bad terms lapses {rules.allies.lapse|pct} of the time each season, unless one guarantees the other.

A nation can unite with a smaller nation of its own people by treaty once their relations reach {rules.unite.relations} and it is more than {rules.unite.power|times} as powerful, unless the smaller one has another great power for an ally.
When a people is united, unrest falls by {rules.unite.calm} across the new nation, and the provinces of its people are integrated at once.
Great powers: The {rules.majors.count|word} strongest nations are the great powers, recounted every {rules.majors.every|span}.
Economy: Every province beyond the first {rules.admin.free|word} costs its nation {rules.admin.cost|pct} of all its gold a year, until it keeps no more than {rules.admin.floor|pct} of it.

The first factory in a province costs {rules.price.factory} gold, and each one after it {rules.price.factoryGrowth|times} the one before; a province holds at most {rules.build.maxFactories} factories. A nation behind the most industrial one pays up to {rules.price.copy|pct} less, copying what others built.
Raising the army costs {rules.price.recruit} gold per thousand men, and keeping it {rules.price.upkeep} gold per thousand men a season.
A nation builds {rules.build.slots.base|word} thing at a time, and one more for every {rules.build.slots.per|word} provinces it holds. Each season it does up to {rules.actions|word} things.
Each season a province's people grow by {rules.growth.base|fine}, and {rules.growth.perFactory|fine} more for every factory.
A nation in debt angers its people: {rules.debt.unrest} unrest everywhere. More than {rules.debt.below|abs} gold in debt, it also loses {rules.debt.army|down} of its army every season.
Wars: Each war keeps a tally of the land each side occupies and the battles it wins. Only the armies of nations that border land they could take or free fight its battles, and only they suffer the losses: an ally with no reachable front adds nothing and loses nothing. A side wins when its tally reaches {rules.war.win} ({rules.war.greatWin} in the {events.greatWar.name}), but no war ends in its first {rules.war.minSeasons|word} seasons unless one side holds all of the other's land.

After {rules.war.seasons|word} seasons ({rules.war.greatSeasons|word} in the {events.greatWar.name}) a war ends anyway: a side ahead by more than {rules.war.timeoutLead} wins, otherwise it is a white peace. From {rules.war.stalemate.after|word} seasons on, a war with neither side ahead by {rules.war.stalemate.below} ends in a white peace {rules.war.stalemate.chance|pct} of the time each season.

The winner takes the war goal if it can reach it, and up to {rules.war.extra|word} more occupied province{rules.war.extra|s} ({rules.war.greatExtra|word} in the {events.greatWar.name}) that it has a claim on, or any it occupies once its tally reaches {rules.war.crushing}. The loser pays {rules.war.reparations|pct} of its gold, shared by the winners who gained no land. Then the two sides keep the peace for {rules.war.truce|span}.
A nation whose unrest averages {rules.war.maxUnrest} or more starts no war.
An army fights {rules.battle.industry|pct} harder for every factory its provinces hold on average.

Every battle kills {rules.battle.dead|fine} of the province's people and wrecks one of its factories {rules.battle.ruin|pct} of the time, and an occupied province gains {rules.battle.occupied} unrest. Each season of war the side that wins the battle loses {rules.battle.losses.win.0|fine} to {rules.battle.losses.win.1|fine} of its army, the other side {rules.battle.losses.lose.0|fine} to {rules.battle.losses.lose.1|fine}.

A province won in war loses a factory, if it has one. If its people are the conqueror's own or accepted, it starts {rules.conquest.kin.integrated|pct} integrated with at least {rules.conquest.kin.unrest} unrest; if not, {rules.conquest.other.integrated|pct} and {rules.conquest.other.unrest}. A province gained by treaty is at most {rules.conquest.treaty|pct} integrated.
Each season a province becomes {rules.integrate.kin|pct} more integrated if its people are the ruler's own or accepted, and {rules.integrate.other|fine} if not.
Uprisings: Riots that the garrison puts down leave the province at {rules.uprising.crushed.unrest} unrest and cost the ruler {rules.uprising.crushed.army|down} of his army.

An uprising of the ruler's own people is a revolution: the ruler falls, the nation loses {rules.uprising.revolution.gold|frac} its gold and {rules.uprising.revolution.army|down} of its army, and unrest falls by {rules.uprising.revolution.calm} everywhere, to no less than {rules.uprising.revolution.floor}.

A province that rises next to a nation of its own people joins it at {rules.uprising.joins.unrest} unrest. Whenever a province breaks away, every province of a subject people left in the old nation gains {rules.uprising.spread} unrest.

Rebels who find no allies are beaten back at a heavy price: the province stays at {rules.uprising.alone.unrest} unrest, and its ruler loses {rules.uprising.alone.army|down} of his army and {rules.uprising.alone.gold|down} of his gold.
A province that wins its independence starts at {rules.uprising.free.unrest} unrest and fully integrated, and the old ruler loses {rules.uprising.free.army|down} of his army.
Development: Every living nation receives a development offer in {advances.season|season} of {advances.years|list}, using the game calendar. The opening player offer follows the opening ruler choice. There are no retrospective awards for missed opportunities.

Each offer contains one eligible, unowned advance from each category: {advances.categories.military.name}, {advances.categories.economy.name} and {advances.categories.government.name}. Identities are random within categories; an unavailable category is filled from the remaining eligible pool without duplicates.
The player must choose one face-up card and the game pauses until resolved. AI nations receive equivalent offers and choose randomly. Advances cost no gold and cannot be rerolled.

Each offered card independently draws its rarity: {rarities.0.name} {rarities.0.odds|pct}, {rarities.1.name} {rarities.1.odds|pct}, {rarities.2.name} {rarities.2.odds|pct}, {rarities.3.name} {rarities.3.odds|pct}, {rarities.4.name} {rarities.4.odds|pct}. Rarity strengthens the same effects without adding grants or penalties. Every advance has one or two effects at every rarity, with no added grants, penalties or levels.

Advances belong to the nation and survive ruler changes. Each can be acquired only once, regardless of rarity, with no upgrades or replacements. Percentage modifiers multiply with other advances and the ruler; planning years add. Costs stay positive through multiplication.

Coast cards require a coastal province; border cards require a living neighbour. Targeted cards require a living neighbouring non-ally and name a fixed target when offered, preferring the rival, otherwise the strongest eligible neighbour. The target strength bonus applies only against that nation; casualty reductions apply to every battle.

Core-land strength applies only in wars whose goal is the nation’s core land, whether defending or recovering it. General speed and foreign-province speed both apply only when a conquest belongs to an unaccepted people outside core land. Strength changes effectiveness, never army headcount; faster progress is not a reduction of time by the same percentage.
Advances add no orders or new objectives: the same ministers forecast decisions in gold, with the existing costs of growth. After the final scheduled opportunity there are no further timed offers.
